title: Playlist and Mixtape
premise: Ada Crane, a scholarship student counting down the days to graduation at Ashgrove Academy, is added to a mysterious group chat called Playlist and Mixtape that begins predicting events before they happen — a fire drill, a broken window, a classmate's disappearance. As the predictions escalate from eerie to dangerous, Ada and four classmates discover the chat is run by someone using their own private messages against them, forcing each to confront who they are when their carefully constructed labels are stripped away. In the end, Ada exposes the orchestrator — her closest friend, who built the chat to force the truth about a shared buried secret into the open — and chooses honesty over loyalty, walking into prom unmasked.
about_author: Silas Ishikawa is the pen name of a former boarding school teacher who spent six years listening to teenagers trade secrets in hallways. They write stories about the moment friendship becomes something you have to choose rather than inherit.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Establishes Ada as the scholarship kid timing everything — classes, meals, her sentence at Ashgrove — and introduces her tight friend group: loyal Theo, polished Priya, chaotic Juno, and quiet Marcus. A strange group chat invitation appears on her phone. Beat: restless anticipation.

chapters.title: Side A
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The chat sends its first 'prediction': a fire drill at 2:14 PM. It happens exactly. The group laughs it off as a prank, but Ada notices the message used her private nickname for the east stairwell. Beat: unease beneath humor.

chapters.title: B-Sides
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, hiding that his scholarship depends on rowing results he's faking, receives a prediction about his own secret. He tells no one. Beat: guilt compounding into isolation.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, the perfect head girl candidate, gets a prediction exposing her forged recommendation letter. She suspects the others and starts quietly investigating their phones. Beat: paranoia dressed as competence.

chapters.title: Interlude: Detention
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. All five land in detention together after a predicted vandalism incident they didn't commit. Trapped in one room, old loyalties surface, and Ada realizes whoever runs the chat knows things only friends would know. Beat: suspicion turning inward.

chapters.title: Skip Track
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno, the group's comic relief, admits to Ada she received a prediction about her brother's overdose last spring — something already happened. The chat isn't predicting; it's replaying. Beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Ada and Marcus break into the school's dead media lab, where the chat's IP traces. They find burned CDs labeled with each of their names and a photo of the five of them from freshman year — before Marcus transferred in. Beat: dread of being known.

chapters.title: Marcus
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus confesses he was at Ashgrove freshman year under a different name and left after an incident the group has collectively forgotten — or been made to forget. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Remix
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds the chat's messages mirror real texts the five exchanged years ago, word for word. Someone archived everything. She confronts Ada instead of reporting it, choosing self-protection over truth. Beat: loyalty bending toward betrayal.

chapters.title: Dropout
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's fake rowing results are posted publicly by the chat; he loses his scholarship path. He lashes out at the group, accusing Ada of running it because she 'needs' them all gone. Beat: fracture.

chapters.title: Low Battery
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Isolated and exhausted, Ada rereads her own archived messages and finds gaps — memories that don't match the transcripts. Someone edited the record, including her memory of the incident Marcus mentioned. Beat: vertigo of unreliable self.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The chat predicts prom will 'end like last time.' The group realizes there was a previous prom incident, erased from school records. Juno remembers fragments: a fire, a girl named Wren nobody mentions anymore. Beat: buried history surfacing.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada tracks down Wren, now living two towns over, who confirms the five of them — plus Wren — caused the fire that got Marcus expelled and Wren withdrawn. The group agreed to forget; the agreement itself was documented. Beat: shame made concrete.

chapters.title: Mute All
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the chat account was created with school admin credentials — meaning a student with access, or a teacher. Her investigation points at Theo, whose alibi collapses. Beat: wrong answer arriving convincingly.

chapters.title: The Longest Track
chapters.summary: Group POV rotation. The five convene in the media lab to compare notes and realize every accusation circles back to someone who knew all of them intimately. Trust is nearly zero, but staying apart means being picked off. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Feedback Loop
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada sets a trap: feeds a false secret into the group and watches which version appears in the chat. The trap works — but the reply quotes a detail only present in a conversation Ada had alone with Juno. Beat: heartbreak of deduction.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Cornered, Juno confesses: she built the chat with help from Wren, using the archive Wren kept. She wanted them to remember what they did to her brother — Wren's fire was set to cover his drug buys for the group. Beat: grief weaponized into control.

chapters.title: Fade Out
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Juno escalates: final prediction says the truth goes public at prom unless the group confesses first. Theo wants to destroy the evidence; Priya wants to negotiate; Marcus wants to disappear again. Ada refuses all three options. Beat: resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Prom Night, Side B
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Prom unfolds under threat; Juno prepares to broadcast the archive mid-slow-dance. Ada intercepts her, and instead of stopping her, takes the microphone herself. Beat: climax — choice over coercion.

chapters.title: Confession Track
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confesses everything to the assembled school — the fire, the cover-up, her own silence — stripping off every label she'd hidden behind. The room's reaction matters less than her own relief. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Bonus Track
chapters.summary: Rotating POVs. Aftermath: Theo owns his failure honestly, Priya withdraws her candidacy, Marcus re-enrolls under his real name, and Wren visits campus. Juno and Ada meet awkwardly, neither forgiven nor exiled. Beat: consequences lived with, not erased.

chapters.title: Playlist and Mixtape
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, final day. Graduation arrives; Ada deletes the countdown app she's used since freshman year. She makes the group a mixtape — not of predictions, but of songs from the year they became honest. Beat: quiet hope, identity chosen.
